subtitle: A design leader who still builds — AI in production, and the maturity work underneath it

bio.short: I lead design functions and I still build. The last year went into AI that runs in production — a support copilot, a fundraising system I built end to end, and prototypes engineering ships from. Before that, fifteen years raising UX maturity at Ninox, Datameer and Spreadshirt.
bio.long:
The clearest thing to look at is the support copilot at Bibel TV. It drafts replies to viewer letters from the service handbook. Most of the design was deciding what it must not do. Restricted topics are enforced in the output rather than left to the model to remember. Messages in crisis escalate to a person instead of being drafted. The send decision never leaves a human. It went out fully optional, so it had to earn its place on the hard cases.

The fundraising system I built alone, end to end: the analysis, the prompt architecture, the prototype, then the production skill. And the practice underneath both is agentic engineering — I prototype in real code against real APIs, and engineering ships from that code. Around 70% of what the model writes lands, and iteration moved from days to hours. Engineering at Bibel TV is an external agency, so that handoff crosses a company boundary and holds anyway. There are no direct reports in this role. It is function leadership and practice change rather than headcount, and it is worth saying so plainly.

The longer thread is maturity. At Ninox I ran a collaborative self-assessment rather than imposing a model, established design as a function co-equal with product and engineering, and sat on the Senior Leadership Team with five reports including a design lead. I hired two, promoted two and let two go, covered Head of Product from July to October 2023, and hired the consultant who was then brought in to hold it. At Datameer I moved design from an execution function to a strategic partner and got executive support for research, including the screening method that reached analysts working inside banks. At Spreadshirt I scaled an assessment framework across a 200-plus-person matrix organisation.

context.company: DocuWare — document digitisation and workflow automation for enterprise, sold across many industries. Germering (Munich), New York, Sofia. Headcount not stated anywhere in the posting.
context.role: Director of User Experience, accountable for Research and Design, leading UX leaders across both. The posting rules out two shapes explicitly: 'a build-and-scale role, not a maintenance one… a maker and a leader who leads through the work — not a strategy-only or people-management-only role.'
context.emphasis: Lead with AI shipped into production and the trust decisions that made it shippable, because 'a maker who leads through the work' is the sentence in this posting written for him. Then UX maturity advanced three times, each with a named method, which is the honest form of scaling available here. Then the full range of people decisions at Ninox, including two promotions and the Head of Product hire.
context.avoid: Never say scaled, grew or built out about a team. No team he has led has ever grown in headcount, anywhere — confirmed 2026-08-11, not merely unevidenced. Never claim a budget beyond the €20k ChurchDesk project; there is no function budget. Never present Datameer as work inside a growing organisation: it went back into startup mode. Ninox and Spreadshirt were growing. Never offer the Head of Product hire as evidence of managing a manager — the successor became a peer. Never name him or any colleague on this page. Never imply he has managed a researcher; he owns the research practice and has never had a researcher report to him. Education is the completed M.A. and nothing more.
